title: BOAC 777
summary: The Douglas DC-3 departed Lisbon for Bristol on 1 June 1943 and was attacked by eight German Junkers Ju 88 fighter aircraft approximately 200 miles northwest of the Spanish coast. The aircraft crashed into the Bay of Biscay with all 17 occupants killed, including actor Leslie Howard and several British passengers believed to be spies. German motivations for the attack remain unclear, though one theory suggests they believed British Prime Minister Winston Churchill was aboard.
probable_cause: The aircraft was attacked by eight German Junkers Ju 88 fighter planes. The attack occurred during an intensification of air combat over the Bay of Biscay in 1943, though the specific reason for targeting this aircraft remains undetermined.

title: Bakers Creek air crash
summary: Boeing B-17C took off from Mackay Airfield in foggy conditions on 14 June 1943 headed for Port Moresby. Flames were observed along the fuselage and wings shortly after takeoff. The aircraft made a low-altitude turn and crashed near Bakers Creek, Queensland, killing 40 of 41 people aboard. The cause of the crash remains undetermined.

title: American Airlines 63 (Flagship Ohio)
summary: Flight 63 cruised at 2,000-2,500 ft on the Louisville-Nashville leg when thunderstorms around Smiths Grove produced extreme turbulence and strong downdrafts that forced the aircraft to lose altitude. The DC-3 descended until it struck trees, then slid across an open field. Two passengers survived; all four crew members perished.
probable_cause: The extreme turbulence and conditions caused by the nearby thunderstorm created such severe flying conditions that the pilot was unable to maintain control of the aircraft.
